summary.oneLiner: Justo has rebounded from FY24 disruption caused by promoter exit and stalled approvals, now leveraging a 94% repeat developer base and new tech platforms to drive 30-40% revenue growth; the upcoming entry into three new cities and Chesterton JV unlocks a $1.5B+ addressable market beyond its current 1% penetration in Pune/Mumbai.

one-line thesis: Justo has rebounded from FY24 disruption caused by promoter exit and stalled approvals, now leveraging a 94% repeat developer base and new tech platforms to drive 30-40% revenue growth; the upcoming entry into three new cities and Chesterton JV unlocks a $1.5B+ addressable market beyond its current 1% penetration in Pune/Mumbai.
financial scorecard: Revenue: ₹90Cr (FY25 est.) (+10% YoY); EBITDA: ~25% margin (stable); PAT (reported): ₹20Cr (FY25 est.) (+30% YoY); PAT (normalized): ₹15.3Cr (FY24) → ₹20Cr (FY25); Order Book: ₹7,929Cr (incl. ₹3,000Cr expected in Q4); Net Debt: Negative cash flow from ops due to 6-month collection cycle; One-offs: FY24 PAT dip due to promoter exit and halted launches; FY25 recovery driven by cleared environmental approvals and IPO capital.
guidance: Revenue growth: 30-40% YoY to ₹125Cr+ in FY26; Margin: Sustain 25% EBITDA; Order inflow: ₹5,000Cr FY26 (₹3,500Cr existing + ₹1,500Cr new); Capex/Commissioning: ₹150-200Cr for tech AI/ML upgrades and Chesterton JV setup, primarily FY26.
order book & pipeline: 44 active mandates worth ₹4,000-5,000Cr; total inventory pipeline at ₹7,929Cr (incl. ₹3,000Cr expected in Q4); 50%+ execution expected in FY26.
segment / subsidiary detail: Pune: 73% revenue (avg. ticket ₹80L-1Cr); Mumbai: 23% revenue (avg. ticket ₹1.2-1.3Cr); Commercial: 6-7 months old, low contribution; Advisory: ₹5-6Cr FY25, to be replaced by Chesterton JV; New markets (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad) to contribute from FY26.
growth verticals / optionality: Entry into Bangalore (Q1FY26), Ahmedabad (Q2FY26), Hyderabad (Q4FY26); Chesterton JV for capital markets/JV/JDA advisory; New verticals in villas and plotting; AI/ML customer targeting to reduce CAC by 30-40%; potential ESOP rollout for retention.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin ~25% (stable); 75% of costs are employee-related (salaries, incentives); broker payouts account for 2.5-3% of GMV; fixed overheads high due to 500+ employees; cost leverage expected as revenue scales and AI reduces lead acquisition cost.
capex / expansion: ₹150-200Cr allocated for AI/ML enhancement of Justo Verse/Works, CRM integration, and Chesterton JV setup; no major property capex; all tech investments are software and platform-based.
capital allocation: IPO proceeds used to fund tech upgrades and Chesterton JV; no dividends paid; focus on reinvestment in AI, market expansion, and ESOPs; no debt-funded acquisitions planned.
risks & watch-items: Regulatory delays in environmental/CC approvals; high employee attrition at junior levels; over-reliance on Pune/Mumbai (73%/23%); delayed receivables (180-day DSO); Chesterton JV execution risk; competition from Anarock/Xanadu.
management quality / tone: Confident, data-driven, and execution-focused; CEO emphasizes professional governance, tech superiority, and repeat developer relationships; acknowledges past disruption but frames FY26 as inflection point with clear roadmap; tone is bullish on scalability and AI potential.
non-obvious takeaways: Justo’s 94% repeat developer rate is a hidden moat — developers outsource entire sales ops to them, creating sticky, high-margin relationships; the 180-day DSO is not a credit risk but a structural delay from registration/home loan cycles; Chesterton JV is not just branding — it’s a re-entry of a 220-year-old global firm with 227 offices, giving Justo instant global credibility and JV deal flow.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Developers struggle with fixed overheads and stalled approvals | Justo Realfintech Limited | beneficiary | High | Justo converts fixed developer costs to variable, mitigates approval delays by only taking RERA-approved projects, and boosts sales velocity via tech-enabled mandates. |
| Home loan disbursement delays hurt developer cash flow | Justo Realfintech Limited | beneficiary | High | Justo’s DSA arm (₹800Cr expected this year) captures loan-related revenue and accelerates collections, strengthening developer loyalty. |
| PropTech firms lack integrated sales + CRM + HR platforms | Justo Realfintech Limited | beneficiary | High | Justo’s proprietary stack (Verse/Works/Pulse) is a defensible moat — no competitor has this full-stack integration. |

themes.title: Flexible workspace, PropTech & commercial real-estate services
themes.need: The GCC build-out and hybrid-work shift drive managed/flexible office demand, and Q1FY27 showed flex becoming the marginal buyer of Indian office space. SMARTWORKS grew revenue 44% to INR 546cr with normalized EBITDA INR 107cr (+74%) at a 19.6% margin, lifted GCC clients from 15% to 21% of revenue in a single quarter, and reported India's highest-ever quarterly leasing at 24.6 mn sq ft with 27% of it through flex, up from 19% a year ago. PropTech consolidation started in the same quarter: AURUM announced the acquisition of Housing.com (~24% of India's online-portal share, 58mn monthly visits) at ~1.5x revenue against listed comparables at 4.5-10x, with Housing currently burning ~INR 200cr a year and committed to break even in four to six quarters. AWFIS/EFCIL/INDIQUBE/DEVX/WEWORK add managed workspace; NIRLON on office REIT-proxy assets.
themes.driver: GCC seat-count additions and flex share of net leasing; AURUM's four-to-six-quarter Housing.com breakeven clock; enterprise managed-office wins.
